messages:
siva: Heads-up: ran a probe on prefetch-aware cohorting tonight. Observed KV prefetch thrash when small prompts (<50 tokens) are mixed with long-context streaming. Dumping notes.

maya: Nice. Can you paste perf numbers? 99p latencies, batch sizes, kernel flips? :eyes:

siva: ```
probe: 2026-03-16 02:12
cfg: token_budget=512, queue_policy=short-first=0.7
stats: mean_batch=6, 95p=85ms, 99p=230ms, tail_mem=8.2GB
kv-prefetch: hits=72%, evictions/sec=1.3
kernel-switches/sec=0.8
```

olga: That's a pretty big 99p. Did kernel selection thrash because sequence length variance triggered different kernel paths?

siva: Yes. Long decode-rate prompts (>=2.5 tok/s) caused the runtime to prefer the streaming kernel which uses different attention tiling. When short prompts got binned into the same queue, we saw kernel cache misses and evictions.

noah: Can we try classification by decode-rate buckets + lock kernel per batch? e.g., only form batches from requests that map to the same kernel candidate.

maya: Also consider token-budget per queue. If we set a lower budget for short-prompt cohort we should reduce KV churn. What's the prefetch window doing right now?

siva: Ran a quick sim: token_budget_short=128 reduces mean_batch to 4 but 99p drops to ~120ms; evictions/sec down to 0.4. Throughput hit ~6% (side effect). Worth it for tail-sensitive SLAs.

olga: Sounds like an acceptable tradeoff for interactive endpoints. We should quantify cost delta though.

siva: Suggested queue policy config (pooled YAML sample):
```
queue_policies:
  - name: short_cohort
    length_max: 60
    decode_rate_max: 1.5
    token_budget: 128
    prefer_kernel: 'dense-small-tiling'
  - name: streaming_cohort
    decode_rate_min: 1.5
    token_budget: 512
    allow_kernel: ['streaming','dense-large']
```

noah: We should add a canary: lock kernel-per-batch + short_cohort budget on a single rack, add tracing tags for kernel_id, kv_evictions and decode_rate bucket.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: ring=1, nodes=3, config=queue-prefetch-v2 (ETA ~15m) :rocket:

maya: I'll spin up a perf dashboard that shows 50/95/99 latencies, kernel-switches/sec, kv-evictions/sec and mean_batch. Also will add alerts on 99p regression >20%.

siva: Thanks — I'll open a PR with the config and a unit test for the classifier boundary cases (length/ decode_rate ties). Will attach benchmark outputs to the PR.
